question: What is the primary function of an Electronic Health Record?

options.A: To track financial profits generated by specific hospital wards
options.B: To eliminate the need for physical hospital buildings entirely
options.C: To store digital patient data for sharing across providers
options.D: To replace human nursing assessments with automated computer scripts

explanation: EHRs are built primarily to compile and share comprehensive patient data securely among different healthcare facilities and team members. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why does an EHR improve multi-disciplinary team communication?

options.A: It gives all authorized clinical staff instant access to live patient notes
options.B: It removes the legal requirement for nurses to document care
options.C: It automatically orders medications without requiring doctor approval
options.D: It translates medical jargon into local Nigerian languages automatically

explanation: Instant accessibility ensures that doctors, nurses, and pharmacists view the exact same real-time clinical status during shift handovers. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h1)

question: What was a major disadvantage of traditional paper health records?

options.A: They could only be accessed using specialized computer software
options.B: They automatically deleted old nursing notes after twenty-four hours
options.C: They were easily misplaced and often featured illegible handwriting
options.D: They required continuous electrical power supply to remain readable

explanation: Paper files frequently went missing within hospital archives, and poor handwriting contributed heavily to clinical miscommunication. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h2)

question: How does transitioning to digital records directly assist daily nursing duties?

options.A: It allows nurses to diagnose complex diseases without doctors
options.B: It reduces the time spent searching for misplaced physical files
options.C: It completely removes the responsibility of charting vital signs
options.D: It guarantees that patients never experience medication side effects

explanation: Eliminating physical archive searches frees up more direct patient care hours for nurses on busy wards. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the function of Clinical Decision Support tools within an EHR?

options.A: To track patient feeding times in the hospital canteen
options.B: To manage the hospital budget and order general office supplies
options.C: To provide automated alerts regarding drug interactions and allergies
options.D: To schedule annual leave for nursing personnel automatically

explanation: Clinical Decision Support software actively flags potential safety hazards like allergic reactions before medications are administered. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why is system interoperability critical for modern electronic health records?

options.A: It allows separate healthcare facilities to share patient data seamlessly
options.B: It stops computer viruses from infecting hospital databases
options.C: It ensures that nurses can print physical paper charts faster
options.D: It prevents patients from viewing their own laboratory results

explanation: Interoperability bridges communication gaps so that a patient's history follows them accurately between different hospitals. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is a key characteristic that distinguishes an EHR from an EMR?

options.A: An EMR requires internet access while an EHR functions completely offline
options.B: An EHR is designed to share data across multiple healthcare organizations
options.C: An EHR can only be used by physicians and excludes nursing notes
options.D: An EMR contains lifelong records from every hospital in the country

explanation: EHRs surpass single-clinic EMRs by facilitating broad, cross-facility data exchange and long-term tracking. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h4)

question: A clinic installs software that only digitizes local patient charts without sharing them externally. What have they installed?

options.C: An automated clinical decision support portal

explanation: Standalone software restricted to a single practice functions as an EMR rather than a fully interoperable EHR. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h4)

question: How do EHRs directly contribute to enhanced patient safety during medication administration?

options.A: By automatically injecting drugs without human verification
options.B: By eliminating errors caused by illegible handwritten prescriptions
options.C: By allowing nurses to bypass the doctor's prescription entirely
options.D: By testing medications on patients before they leave the pharmacy

explanation: Clear digital text prevents dangerous misinterpretations of drug names and dosages common in handwritten notes. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which benefit do nurses experience when conducting admission assessments with an EHR?

options.A: Guaranteed elimination of all documentation duties on the ward
options.B: Automatic authorization to discharge patients without a doctor
options.C: Instant access to past medical history and previous lab results
options.D: Exemption from performing physical head-to-toe examinations

explanation: Digital records allow nurses to quickly review prior health data, streamlining the initial patient assessment process. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is a major infrastructural challenge facing EHR adoption in Nigeria?

options.A: Unreliable electrical power supply and frequent grid failures
options.B: An overabundance of high-speed internet causing network crashes
options.C: A complete absence of computers in the entire country
options.D: Legislation that strictly forbids storing health data digitally

explanation: Inconsistent electricity poses a constant threat to digital systems, necessitating expensive alternative power solutions. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why can staff resistance to change stall an EHR project in a hospital?

options.A: Technicians lock all hospital doors to prevent nurses from working
options.B: Ministry regulations fine hospitals that transition to electronic charts
options.C: Workers automatically demand higher salaries whenever a computer is turned on
options.D: Staff accustomed to paper charts may struggle or refuse to adopt digital workflows

explanation: Habituated routines create friction during digital transitions, making comprehensive staff training and change management essential. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is an effective method to restrict unauthorized access to patient EHR accounts?

options.A: Leaving all computer terminals unlocked in busy public corridors
options.B: Implementing role-based user permissions and unique login credentials
options.C: Writing staff passwords on sticky notes attached to computer screens
options.D: Permitting any hospital visitor to view files upon verbal request

explanation: Unique logins and role-based restrictions ensure that personnel access only the specific patient files required for their role. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h7)

question: What responsibility does a nurse hold regarding EHR security on a busy ward?

options.A: Allowing patients to type their own clinical progress notes
options.B: Logging out of computer workstations when leaving the terminal unattended
options.C: Sharing personal login details with students to speed up charting
options.D: Disabling system encryption to make the computer run faster

explanation: Leaving a terminal active invites unauthorized access, compromising patient confidentiality and accountability for documentation. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h7)

question: How might artificial intelligence integrated into future EHRs assist clinical nurses?

options.A: By analyzing vital signs to predict patient deterioration before crises occur
options.B: By writing hospital discharge summaries without checking patient charts
options.C: By administering intravenous medications automatically without oversight
options.D: By completely replacing the need for bedside physical nursing assessments

explanation: AI algorithms can detect subtle warning trends in continuous data, alerting nurses to intervene early. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h8)

question: What is a predicted development for mobile health tools in future nursing practice?

options.A: Requiring nurses to carry heavy paper folders during community outreach
options.B: Eliminating all forms of documentation in surgical and medical wards
options.C: Stopping all communication between doctors and nursing staff
options.D: Recording bedside observations directly onto portable tablets or wearables

explanation: Mobile devices enable real-time point-of-care charting right at the patient's bedside, improving workflow efficiency. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h8)
